top_ai_signals.name: Metadata & Provenance
top_ai_signals.summary: The file's embedded provenance marks it as AI-generated.
top_ai_signals.what_found: The provenance metadata flags this as trained-algorithmic (AI-generated) media.
top_ai_signals.why_it_matters: Provenance markers like C2PA are an industry-standard, hard-to-fake trace written by the generator itself. Finding one is among the strongest provenance signals available.
top_ai_signals.caveat: Provenance can be stripped or, rarely, forged. Absence of a marker is not proof of authenticity.

top_ai_signals.name: Spectral Artifacts
top_ai_signals.summary: The Six-Lens model scored this image 83.7% AI / 16.3% authentic — a extremely high-confidence finding toward synthetic generation.
top_ai_signals.what_found: All six spectral lenses — visual texture (ConvNeXt), frequency grids (FFT), sensor noise simulation (SRM), color-space fingerprints (YCbCr), spatial reconstruction (SPAI), and robustness testing — collectively scored this image 83.7% AI. A score this strong, the majority of lenses independently flagged patterns like periodic frequency grids and noise distributions inconsistent with any known camera sensor profile.
top_ai_signals.why_it_matters: This model looks for patterns invisible to the human eye — buried in the pixel-level math of the image. A 83.7% score means the statistical fingerprint aligns significantly more with AI generation than camera physics, and these frequency-domain traces are very hard to remove without visibly degrading the image.
top_ai_signals.caveat: Heavy JPEG compression, aggressive resizing, or strong image filters can partially destroy the frequency-domain signals this model depends on, potentially softening a confident AI detection into an inconclusive result. Conversely, very new or unusual AI generators not present in training data may produce lower-than-expected scores.

This balanced exposure is realistic-looking but not diagnostic - it fits equally well for a careful real photograph and a modern AI generator.
top_inconclusive_signals.why_it_matters: Lighting is most useful when it's either suspiciously perfect (AI) or clearly clipping (real). A balanced middle-ground doesn't give us enough to work with, so this signal defers to others.
top_inconclusive_signals.caveat: HDR post-processing, tone mapping, strong flash, and professional retouching can all alter exposure profiles - introducing 'AI-like' qualities into real photos or vice versa.

The compression stress is consistent across all four quadrants, and only 0.00% of pixels show elevated residuals. This uniform profile suggests the image has a consistent compression history - no obvious signs of region-level editing or compositing.
top_inconclusive_signals.why_it_matters: A uniform ELA profile removes one red flag - there are no obvious editing seams. However, ELA does not tell us whether the image is AI-generated, only that it has not been obviously composited. The other detectors handle the AI vs. real question.
top_inconclusive_signals.caveat: ELA detects editing and compression inconsistency, not AI generation. Social media uploads, repeated saves, and WhatsApp forwarding all degrade this test. It's treated as a weak supporting check.
